extracted.intended_audience: K-12 social studies teachers and educators (civics, government, U.S. history)
extracted.subtask_description: A landing/catalog page of free K–12 social studies and civics instructional resources, curriculum overviews, primary sources, classroom activities, and student programs produced by the Bill of Rights Institute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Centering on Founding Principles and Civic Virtues
rubrics_metrics.description: Each BRI resources is centered on the Founding Principles and Civic Virtues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Student activities and opportunities emphasize BRI's founding principles and civic virtues; resources include an interactive to teach these principles in a fun and engaging way.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pedagogical approach: narratives, primary sources, and point‑counterpoint debates
rubrics_metrics.description: History is presented through a series of narratives, primary sources, and point-counterpoint debates that invites students to participate in the ongoing conversation about the American experiment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This approach is used across multiple curriculum overviews (e.g., Life, Liberty, and the Pursuit of Happiness; Government & Politics; middle school and elementary curricula) to encourage student participation and critical thinking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of primary sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Resources include primary sources as a core component of instruction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary sources are used alongside narratives and debates to ground lessons in original documents and evidence for classroom analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Current events selection relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Current Events Articles are news articles relevant to topics in U.S. History, Government, and Civics classrooms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selections should directly connect to classroom topics and serve as timely material for discussion and analysis in civics/history lessons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Landmark Supreme Court Cases: majority‑ruling summaries with rights impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Summaries present the majority ruling in landmark Supreme Court cases that have had an impact on our rights as citizens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content focuses on explaining the Court's majority decision and its effects on rights and civic life, suitable for classroom use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student program eligibility and focus — MyImpact Challenge
rubrics_metrics.description: $40,000 in total prizes for students and their teachers for Civic Engagement projects. Open to 13-19 year olds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program targets civic engagement projects from students aged 13–19; prize funding is available to students and their teachers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student program participation/prize — Think The Vote
rubrics_metrics.description: Participate in debates with other students around the country for a chance to win $1,000!
rubrics_metrics.guidance: National student debate competition format; participation and competitive performance are implied criteria for eligibility for the prize.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student Fellowship: leadership development focus
rubrics_metrics.description: A leadership development program for students who want to be active builders of civil society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program is aimed at students demonstrating interest in civic leadership and developing skills to engage in civil society; selection/participation criteria are centered on leadership development goals.
